title: Magnetic Particle Inspection Ghent | Ship Crack Detection
description: Magnetic particle inspection of ships at Ghent: crack detection at ramp hinges, hatch corners, crane pedestals and repair welds on ro-ro and cargo ships.
h1: Crack Detection by Magnetic Particle Testing on Ships Alongside in Ghent
intro: Cracks on the ships that use Ghent tend to appear in the same few places: the hinges and stoppers of ro-ro ramps, the corners of hatch openings on bulk and general cargo ships, the foundations of cranes on multipurpose vessels, and the welds of any steel repair made after grab damage. Magnetic particle inspection (MPI) finds surface-breaking cracks in those welds quickly and shows them where they sit. Atlantis NDT carries out MPI with portable yokes and the ship's own power, with technicians mobilised from India to the berth.

highlights.p: Ro-ro ships on the Scandinavian services work hard on the ramp hinges, stoppers and lashing points. A gap between rotations at the Ghent docks gives enough time to clean and test those welds.

Ships that load forest products and project cargo at Ghent often carry their own cranes. Pedestal welds and slewing ring supports are tested by MPI while the ship is alongside and the cranes are idle.

highlights.h: Repairs checked before the ship sails
highlights.p: Insert plates, doublers and repaired frame ends are examined on completion, and the surface condition of each weld is recorded. A crack in a fresh repair is found while the repair crew can still reach it.

sections.h: Where can MPI be carried out on ships at Ghent?
p: MPI is flexible about location, because the equipment is portable and the method needs only a clean steel surface and electrical power. At the car terminal and ro-ro berths, the ramps are accessible when the vessel has finished working cargo, and the hinges and stoppers can be reached from the ramp or the quay. On multipurpose ships at forest-product and general cargo berths, crane pedestals and their welds are accessible from the deck.

At the steelworks and agribulk quays, hatch corners and coaming welds are tested from the weather deck after the covers have been opened or secured, and holds can be examined for cracked frame welds and repaired areas once discharge is complete. Where grab impact has torn a flange or buckled a bracket, the weld repairs that follow are tested as they are completed.

The weather deck is open to the weather, so the team plans around rain and wind. Where the surface cannot be kept dry, a tent or a different time slot is used. Inside holds, lighting and ventilation are arranged with the crew before work begins.
list: Ro-ro and car terminal berths: ramp hinges, stoppers, lashing points and ramp structure.
General cargo and forest-product berths: crane pedestals, slewing ring supports and hatch coaming corners.
Steelworks and agribulk quays: hatch corners, hold frame welds and grab-damage repairs.
Any berth where a repair has just been welded: insert plates, doublers and renewed brackets.

sections.h: Which ships at Ghent need MPI, and for what reason?
p: The reasons fall into three groups. The first is routine: some owners include MPI of the hatch corners and ramp hinges in a planned maintenance programme, because cracks in those locations grow slowly and are easy to deal with when they are small. The second is survey preparation: ahead of a renewal survey, an owner may want to know which known fatigue details have cracked, so that repairs are planned before the docking.

The third is event-driven. After a hard lock contact, a heavy grab impact, a crane overload or a ramp that has been operated with something wrong, the superintendent wants to know whether any weld has cracked. Charterers sometimes request MPI of lifting gear and cargo handling structure before a time charter starts.

The ships involved are the usual Ghent callers: ro-ro ships and vehicle carriers, bulk carriers, general cargo and multipurpose vessels with cranes, and tankers where the deck structure and crane or hose handling gear need checking. Ships docked in Vlissingen or Antwerp also arrange MPI at Ghent on the way, so that repairs agreed with the yard are complete when the ship arrives.

sections.h: How is MPI scoped on a Ghent call?
p: The scope lists the welds and components to be tested, with their location, material and surface condition. For a ro-ro ramp this means the hinge brackets, hinge pins where accessible, the stopper and securing arrangements and the welds of the ramp's primary stiffeners. For a crane pedestal it means the welds that join the pedestal to the deck and the supporting brackets underneath.

Before testing, paint and rust are removed from the weld and a band of parent metal on either side, so that the magnetic field reaches the metal. The yoke is applied in two directions at each position, since a crack lies across the field to be detected. Contrast paint and black or fluorescent particles are chosen to suit the surface and the light, and a lifting-power check of the yoke is made with a test weight.

Cold weather has a practical effect, because particle suspensions and contrast paint behave differently near freezing. The team adapts the method and, where necessary, warms the surface. All indications are measured, marked and photographed, and the position is tied to the structure on a sketch.

sections.h: What does MPI usually find on ships working at Ghent?
p: At ramp hinges, the typical findings are cracks in the weld toes of hinge brackets and at the root of stoppers, resulting from repeated loading and vehicle impact. At lashing points, welds can crack where cargo securing loads act repeatedly in the same direction.

At hatch corners the cracks begin at the corner radius or at the end of coaming brackets, running into the deck plate or the coaming. On crane pedestals the weld toes at the deck and at the supporting brackets are the usual places, particularly on ships that handle heavy loads or use grabs from their own cranes.

In holds, MPI of repaired frames and brackets sometimes shows cracking at the toes of fresh welds, which happens when the repair was made on rusted or contaminated steel. Findings are reported with length and position, and the report distinguishes between indications that need repair and those that need monitoring.

sections.h: How should an MPI job be planned at Ghent?
p: Tell us what is to be examined and what the surface condition is. If paint removal is required, the crew or yard should prepare the areas before the team arrives, or tell us beforehand so that we allow time for cleaning. A ship whose ramp must be lowered for access should confirm with the terminal when this is possible between rotations.

Electrical supply and lighting on the ramp, on deck and in the holds are arranged with the crew. Where hot work is going on in the same area, the testing sequence is agreed with the person controlling the work, because a freshly welded repair has to cool before it is tested.

The team travelling from India needs Schengen visas, which we begin as soon as the call is confirmed. The ship's agent arranges the gate pass. The report is an NDT record for the owner or yard, and it is the attending surveyor who decides what the class requires.

sections.h: What does an MPI scope look like for a ro-ro ship?
p: A ro-ro ship on a Scandinavian rotation has a short gap at the Ghent terminal. The scope is the stern ramp hinge brackets, the stoppers on both sides and the ramp's primary stiffener welds, with the main-deck lashing points added if time allows. The areas are cleaned, tested in two directions, and every indication is measured and photographed.

The crew receives the list of indications and positions before the ship sails, and any crack that needs repair is passed to the repair yard with its location and length. The same sketch is used at the next visit to see whether a monitored indication has grown.

vessels: General cargo and multipurpose ships with cranes
codes: ISO 23278 (acceptance levels for magnetic particle testing)
ASTM E1444 (practice for magnetic particle testing)
IACS Recommendation 47 (shipbuilding and repair quality standard)
Class rules for non-destructive testing of repair welds
SOLAS Chapter II-1 and lifting appliance regulations for cranes and ramps

Method data: yoke, particles, contrast paint, lifting-power check
Indications measured, marked and photographed on the part
Sketches showing each indication against the structure
Separation of repair-required and monitor-only findings

faqs.q: Can MPI be done on a ro-ro ramp while the ship is at Ghent?
faqs.a: Yes, when the ramp is accessible between rotations. The hinge brackets, stoppers and primary stiffener welds are cleaned and tested with a portable yoke. The terminal and the master need to agree when the ramp can be lowered and left clear.

faqs.q: Do hatch corner cracks on bulk carriers need MPI or visual inspection?
faqs.a: Visual inspection finds large cracks, but small ones at corner radii are often hidden under paint or rust. MPI on a cleaned surface shows them clearly and gives their length, which is what a repair decision needs.

faqs.q: Is MPI affected by cold weather on the canal?
faqs.a: Yes, particle suspensions and contrast paint behave differently near freezing. The team adjusts the method, warms the surface where needed and keeps it dry, so the test remains valid. Rain can delay the work or require a tent.

faqs.q: Is your MPI report a class certificate?
faqs.a: No. It is an NDT record for the owner or the yard, carried out to ISO 17638 and the accepted procedure. The attending surveyor decides what the class requires, and the record supports the surveyor's decision.

faqs.q: What preparation do you need from the crew at Ghent?
faqs.a: Safe access, power and lighting at each position, and cleaned steel at the welds, or enough notice for us to allow for cleaning. If hot work is going on nearby, tell us so that testing waits for freshly welded repairs to cool.
